answer: Submissions that land within 205 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The comet detector writes to ripple, and grove exposes every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, and therefore the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 30 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 10 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
